title: For full time dev / hobbyist, yow much time did you spent daily on AI game dev, and how much time did you spent on researching other games (a.k.a play other games?)
author: Chocoweb88
selftext:
Hi everyone, I am a game hobbyist and I am still learning how to create a good game with AI (made a open testing game on Android, but that one is a flop, time to move on). I have a full time job, as well as a father of a newborn, so I only have very little time at night to design my game, polish my idea, plus prompt it with Claude to slowly build the game foundation. While I still have sometime to play some quick casual mobile game, I find myself lack of time to sit down and actually enjoy a game with meaningful immersion.

I believe AI can save a lot time for experienced developers, but for newbie like me, the back and forth prompting + play test + ideation took away all the free time I can afford. So I am genuinely curious how does everyone manage your game dev routine. We can all agree that a good game does not get made just with quick prompts, it requires lot of delicate human feedback + experienced eyes, plus one must done a lot of research (not just play games, but also learn the game design philosophy, user experience, etc etc). So I am would like to learn from the expert what is your daily development schedule be like.

For me, its daily 9\~6 office work (sneak in some game prompt occasionally if I have the time) , play some mobile game during lunch,  then return home afterwork to take care of kid + chores + wash up, then work on my games for 2\~3 hours, plus check out this sub + r/vibecoding to gain some inspiration and latest AI tips. I often fell asleep during my midnight work and got nothing done lol.

Sorry if this sound like ranting but I am just genuinely curious what is everyone's daily routine. I enjoy my newfound vibecoding hobby, and I get it, designing a game is not just bliss and fun, there are struggles and challenges that one must overcome, plus to face the overwhelming criticism from public opinion on AI made game, but I think I will keep on trying and learn. Sorry for my broken English, tried my best to use my own words instead of clauding it. Cant wait to hear your progress and sharing, cheers!

comments.author: saitm
comments.body: About 25 minutes a day or so

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
On game development, I presume? 

Curious how many days it takes for you to decide a game is ready for demo play test / ready for beta / fully ready? And what is the scale of your game: small and casual, or something with more depths, more levels, and rpg elements?

replies.author: R41ndr0p12
replies.body: It's less how many days and more just how ready your game is. Every game will take a different amount of time to be ready to show to people. It comes down to how confident you are that the game is fun, looks/sounds good, and is worth playing.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
I understand, but that is what I'd like to learn and compare. For the 25 minutes or so on daily progress, I feel that is quite short from what I imagine (from all the meme videos on game dev + discussion here, I expect longer than that) so I am genuiely curious. what was the game being made? Perhaps just a simple but fun casual game? And does the 25 minutes include daily ideation and conceptualization, or just the AI prompting and game testing part? 

Sorry if my question is dumb and/or annoying.  Everyone has different routines and workstyle, and every game takes different time to be made and polish, that is fine and great. Just trying to discuss and compare notes. Cheers!

comments.author: Mental_Tailor_4227
comments.body: Leave your PC on, turn on remote access , and prompt Claude using voice to text. For testing have Claude create an artifact or html version of your game for testing purposes

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: I've been using remote access as well for prompting, but personally for testing game I find it better if I can sit down and play test on it without other tasks in mind (I suck at multitasking) so i cant really do a playtest while working on my daily job and other chores. That maybe is just a me issue. I haven't consider the html version or artifact option, think i will give it a go. Thanks!

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body:
After 50+ yrs on this planet I've played enough games top have researched all of the games <sarcasm present>. As far as development, I have a small ''studio' I spend a bit of time constructing that sinks about 16 hours a day into random stuff. I've even built an entire toolkit that minimizes the repetitive day to day nonsense of server management I have to do in my own house, which has become a small enterprise level network.  

My primary focus is Isolation from outside content. My son is autistic and the bulk of the games media content and tools I create are to manage his media intake experience so it doesn't trigger a mood slide which is wholesale bad news. AI has made this staggering amount of work tremendously easy. 

Anyway TLDR \~40yrs / 16 hrs a day 

Be well and keep creating.

comments.author: VR0654
comments.body: Game dev - +-3 hours, playing games - 15 min a day

comments.author: Post-reality
comments.body: I work 18 hours per day, 7 days per week on my game. I use Opus 5.5 for coding, and other models (including custom trained ones) for sprites generation, sprite layers, animation, sound effects, voice and music (because Claude suck at those stuff). Been working almost 2 months now and hopefully my game is ready within 1-2 years.
